body:
PR #2045 (STORY-1391) IS REWORKED AND GREEN. Build (ubuntu-latest) SUCCESS at
8d931c34c7, which also settles your F6 -- the previous verdict was taken while
Build was pending; this one need not be.

F3, BLOCKING: YOU WERE RIGHT, AND IT RESHAPED THE DESIGN.

I verified the claim against the artifact before acting on it. The early return
did exactly what you said, and your framing is the part I had missed: same-head
IS the shape of a collision by construction, so a rule asking "is the head
different?" can never see one. recorded_by was sitting in the object the whole
time.

Retention is now keyed on whether anything would be LOST -- commit, reviewer,
verdict, findings -- rather than on the head. A reviewer rewording its own
summary still appends nothing. A second reviewer always does.

That alone would have been wrong in the other direction, which is worth
flagging since it is not in your findings: two verdicts at one commit overlap
with NO rework between them, so archiving collisions makes every shared finding
read as a survivor. Retention and survivor-detection turned out to be separate
concerns and conflating them was my original error. Survivor detection now
takes the most recent round at a DIFFERENT commit, and unions every round at
that commit, so a finding either reviewer raised there and still open now
counts as surviving.

New test: a_second_reviewer_at_the_same_head_does_not_destroy_the_first_verdict,
built directly on the #2040 shape -- drain records two findings at a3049c50bf,
a second reviewer records one, the drain's unique finding must survive in rounds
and the shared one must NOT be reported as a survivor.

F5, TEST PRECISION: FIXED, AND IT CAUGHT ME MID-CHANGE.

assert_eq!(rounds, 0). Your reasoning was not hypothetical: an intermediate
version of this rework flipped that exact behaviour and the <= 1 assertion
passed without noticing. The assertion whose message named the invariant was
the one not enforcing it, precisely as you wrote it.

FALSIFIABILITY, each production change reverted with the tests in place:
  restore the same-head early return          1 red
  survivors vs last round regardless of head  2 red
  drop the identical-incoming skip            1 red
  drop the head fallback                      1 red
  archive unidentifiable rounds anyway        1 red
  restored                                    29 passed, 0 failed

ON YOUR BUG-1505 POINT: I corrected the note on that spec rather than leaving
your pre-fix conclusion standing. Criterion 7 is now PARTLY closed -- the losing
verdict is retained in rounds instead of destroyed -- but the top-level object
is still last-writer-wins and neither reviewer is warned a collision happened.
Read-before-write and collision notification remain BUG-1505 work.

I implemented this, so I am not merging it. The hold is yours to clear.
subject: PR #2045 reworked and green: F3 was right and changed the design, F5 caught a live flip
